Sets the 256 colors that a [Graphics](Graphics) or [Graphics3D](Graphics3D) window with a depth of 8 shows. The picture is a lookup table of 16 by 16 pixels, and the pixel at x,y is the color with the number y * 16 + x. Drawing happens in full color; the picture of the window, and what ReadPixel and the other commands read from the front and back buffer, have the color of the palette that is nearest (the smallest distance in red, green and blue). With [Dither](Dither) on, the noise that is added before the nearest color is picked is one step of the palette for each channel, so that gradients become a pattern instead of bands. The default palette has all colors of 3 bits of red, 3 of green and 2 of blue, from 0,0,0 to 255,255,255, in the order of the bits RRRGGGBB. GraphicsPallet can be called before or after Graphics and changes what is shown with the next picture. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original has no such command, and its palette modes are not supported. See [Color depth](Color-Depth).
@param imagefile  A picture file of exactly 16 by 16 pixels (any format that LoadImage reads), or an empty string for the default palette. Any other size stops the program with an error message.
